description: Deterministic rules that decide, for each tool call a model proposes, whether it runs (`allow`), waits for a human (`ask`) or is refused (`deny`).
Rules are checked deny first, then ask, then allow, and the first match wins regardless of specificity. An allow rule cannot override a matching deny rule.
A call no rule covers becomes a question for a human, never a silent allow.
Path wildcards where `*` stays inside one path segment and `**` crosses directories: `src/*` matches `src/a.ts` but not `src/lib/a.ts`.
Resolving `.` and `..` segments before matching, so `src/../.env` is checked as `.env`.
Several shell commands joined by `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` or newlines. Each part is evaluated and the strictest decision wins.
When the harness cannot classify a call (unparseable arguments, an unknown tool), it denies or asks instead of allowing.
Humans approving prompts without reading because they arrive too often; fixed by moving frequent safe calls to `allow`.
